title: 35.2 A Spatial-Domain Compressive-Sensing Photoacoustic Imager with Matrix-Multiplying SAR ADC
problem: Wearable deep-tissue photoacoustic (PA) imaging requires low-power, compact receive architecture with integrated data compression for real-time streaming and long-term monitoring, but PA signals are 10x smaller than ultrasound due to optical excitation inefficiency.
motivation: Wearable PA imaging enables preventive healthcare through real-time deep-tissue monitoring (cardiovascular, musculoskeletal, fetal), accessible medical imaging in low-resource settings.
method: The system combines spatial compressive sensing (acquiring measurements of an image space rather than measuring every point separately) with a specialized converter (SAR ADC) that performs matrix multiplication during analog-to-digital conversion. The hardware simultaneously compresses and converts the photoacoustic signal measurements at the sensor itself, avoiding the need for separate compression steps later. Since photoacoustic signals are inherently weak—about 10 times fainter than ultrasound—the converter is optimized with tuned gain, bandwidth, and noise characteristics to reliably capture these faint signals.
key_novelty: A matrix-multiplying SAR ADC integrates compressive sensing directly into analog-to-digital conversion, compressing photoacoustic images at the moment of sensing rather than in a separate step.
contributions: Matrix-multiplying SAR ADC performing simultaneous acquisition and compression
Low-power, compact design suitable for wearable PA imaging
Hardware-integrated compression reducing wireless data bandwidth

metrics.other: Integrated acquisition and compression, wearable form factor

primary_theme: Wearable photoacoustic imager with matrix-multiplying SAR ADC for real-time compression
